env.name: Environment & lighting
env.scope: Skyline, atmosphere, fog, tone mapping, bloom, SSAO, colour grade

issues.text: From the default RTS camera (S2), Arad is still a near-octagon of identical square blocks framed by glowing orange perimeter lines, dropped onto a blank plain. The 'outskirts' are scattered single red and white specks with thin pale scratch lines, which look like debug markers rather than an urban fringe. In S6 the whole town reads as silver-white glitter with flat grey facades. Next to an Age of Empires IV high camera or a Cities: Skylines II night overview, this is the first-glance 'procedural' tell.

The Moab layers are vertical flat curtains with uniform navy fill. From the S7 height they read as stacked paper strips with a hard horizontal top and bottom. The farther ridges are darker than the nearer Moab face, which reverses atmospheric perspective. In S6 the ridge crest is visibly stair-stepped, and in S3 and S6 the plateau edge cuts the rift as a ruler-straight horizontal line, so the escarpment never shows.

A huge intercept flash fills the top of S5, yet every facade is pure black apart from its windows. Only the terrain receives the new flash hemisphere term. Against WARNO and CoH3, where overhead bursts visibly paint roofs and walls, the 'lighting interplay' is missing at the most cinematic moment.

The near desert in S1 and in the lower half of S7 is smeared with large dark, soft streaks that read as cloud shadows or soot on snow, and peppered with blue-black 'ink spot' shrub blobs. In S3 the opposite happens: the plateau is a completely featureless beige plane with no micro-relief or material variety for kilometres. Neither reads as Negev hamada next to CoH3 or Iron Harvest ground.

In the lookout shot the battery apron reads as a navy-blue swimming pool with a hard dark rim, and the boxy launchers sit in it. The Masada road has saturated orange-tan shoulders as wide as the carriageway, so it looks like masking tape on a tabletop.

At tactical zoom the block interiors are large flat beige lots, evenly lit almost like dusk. The new decals are square green or yellow patches that read as placed tiles. The sodium pools exist, but the ground between them isn't dark enough for them to pop the way CoH3 night maps and CS2 do.

Roofs are uniform flat grey slabs with one box and a red dot. In S5 the slabs have balconies, but at S4 zoom the roofs dominate and read as untextured. Rooftop clutter (solar heaters, tanks, parapets) isn't visible at tactical zoom.

env.note: Critic R2: 5/10 (no change). Warmer and layered (S7 depth, S5 windows near CS2), but the town still reads as a game board at S2/S6, Moab ridges are flat sheets, facades go black under flashes, near ground smudgy or blank. Round 3 building.

vfx.name: VFX
vfx.scope: Launches, interceptor trails, intercepts, debris, smoke, screen shake

issues.text: C1/S6: each Arrow kill is a sharp star inside a big, smooth, round glow disc about 180px across at 960px (C1 f00058, f00084). It reads as a lens blob, not a pinpoint flash. After the flash, what remains is a cluster of vertical orange streaks plus pale round dots: a fireworks shower. The canonical S6 frame (t=222.7) lands between kills, so the store-page frame for 'Arrow 3 over the Dead Sea' shows only that drizzle. Broken Arrow and WARNO high-altitude kills are a hard white point with a brief sky lift, then a faint expanding smudge that stays readable for several seconds.

C5 (Nevatim from about 4-5 km): a ballistic warhead hit is a small white dot flash, then a brown lump about 25px wide at 960px. The dust ring is barely visible and no expanding fireball reads. Six seconds later the column is a thin dark wisp (C5 f00095). In S7, the canonical aftermath, the only post-strike smoke is one dark column about 15px wide over Nevatim plus pale puffs along the escarpment. CoH3 heavy artillery and WARNO missile strikes leave large, dark, wind-sheared columns that dominate a tactical-zoom frame.

The ballistic hot trails are constant-width, evenly 'beaded' orange lines (C4 f00064 crop, S5, C5 f00017). They look like tracer or laser beams rather than meteor plasma that sputters and cools. When one passes close to the camera, it renders as a full-height vertical orange pillar with a wide warm wash at the frame edge (C4 f00108, left).

The lingering 'smudge' after each endo kill is an isolated, round, soft grey ball about 25-40px across with a near-circular outline (S5 right of centre, C4 f00108 two blobs mid-sky, C1 pale dots). CoH3 and WARNO post-kill smoke is torn and directional. Round puffs floating alone are the 'sprite-looking puffs' failure sign.
The Arrow 3 boost-phase trails appear only as wide, very faint blue-grey vertical bands on the right of the sky in C1 and S6. They read like searchlight beams or aurora, not lit missile smoke.

Where an Iron Dome trail crests and turns toward the camera, flat blade-like folds with straight edges and thin seam lines are still visible (C3 f00032 top, S3 centre at about x=1040 y=130). Much better than round 1, but a sharp eye still sees polygons.

Measured over 90 frames at the S5 moment (scratch probe of ctx.timings.update.vfx): median 0.6 ms, but p95 2.8 ms and max 6-8 ms, against a 1.5 ms budget. S6 is fine (median 0.3, p95 0.6). The spikes line up with the 40 Hz batched smoke-trail rebuild and smoke-pool update running in the same frame.
David's Sling smoke trails seen from below are still thin white lines, about 3-5px at 1600px (S5 right edge, C4). They are readable now, but not the billowing ribbons of the Dome launch.

vfx.note: Round 3 built: crisp exo star flashes, distance-scaled impacts with smouldering columns, de-lasered ballistic trails, smeared smudges. Critic reviewing.

hud.name: HUD & UX
hud.scope: Alert countdown, objectives, shelter routing — cinematic and minimal

issues.text: Toasts and banners are drawn over the world markers. They are not treated as obstacles, and they sit exactly where the town's markers cluster at the alert camera. In ux-2 the 'Opening West shelter' toast hides a group label. In ux-1 the 'David's Sling deploying' toast sits between the DEPLOY pad and a LOCKED shelter. In ux-3 the 'ALL 92 IN PROTECTED SPACES' banner is crossed by shelter labels (16/24, 8/40) and becomes hard to read. AoE IV and CoH3 never let notification text fight world pins.

At the siren, the things the player must act on are often off-screen or jammed at the screen edge, and nothing points to them. In C2 f00040 the locked Lookout shelter and its 16-person group are wedged into the corner between the clock and the roster, and the second locked shelter (West) is not on screen at all. The roster says LOCKED, but clicking a roster row does not move the camera. The radar shows no shelters or groups. CoH3 and AoE IV use edge arrows and minimap pings for this.

The roster's right column has no right padding: 'LOCKED' and the ETAs (31s, 26s) touch or cross the panel border, and it is worse in compact mode. Feed timestamps are illegible because the row gradient starts fully transparent exactly where <time> sits (23:46 over a road in S2). The barrage subline 'SALVO 2 OF 3 · INTERCEPTS AND FALLING DEBRIS' wraps, leaving 'DEBRIS' as an orphan line in the alert box.

World markers read more like debug tooltips than game pins. Every one is a mono-text box with a 1px stem, and at the S4b wide view or in compact 960x540 the town becomes a field of 14+ boxes with long, crossing leader lines from the 24/48 px lifts. Compact mode zooms the panels to 0.78 but not the markers, so at 960 they dominate (S2-tactical-960). Group feet that drop to 'dot' mode lose all identity. Compare the AoE IV and CoH3 icon-first pins, where text appears on hover or selection.

The pad build popup opens over the air-defence panel and the command bar (ux-0), and marker feet and route rings render under the semi-transparent panels (a group ring under the roster and a diamond between the clock and the roster in C2; the 20/20 pad stem runs into the command bar in S7). The pad label in compact mode shows only '13/20' or 'DEPLOY' with no pad name or battery type.
On the debrief, 'Watch the sky' hides the debrief but leaves .iw-play.dim (opacity 0) on, so the player gets a bare scene with no HUD and no way back to the debrief or to Play again.

The same numbers are framed three ways at once: the roster says 'People outside 92/92', the alert says 'In protected spaces 0/92' and the objective says '0/92'. The debrief says '56/68 threats intercepted' while the AD panel said 86% and the history note says 99%. Each is defensible, but the hierarchy goal is one place per fact.

In compact mode, the AD panel is CSS-zoomed to 0.78, but the radar click handler maps clientX/Y with the unzoomed scale (sc = 226/width), so radar clicks land at the wrong world position below 1100x640.

hud.note: Critic R1: 7/10. Red-alert module near CoH3, start/intro/debrief at AoE IV level; toasts cover markers, no off-screen pointers at the siren, overflows, debug-tooltip markers, small bugs. Round 2 building.
